title: fix(axis-③/arm64 rung-3): C-ABI main trampoline -> crt1 dyn path exits 42 not 0
body: crt_handoff dynamic path exited 0 not 42: hexa fns return a HexaVal pair (x0=tag, x1=payload; TAG_INT=0), and crt1 __libc_start_main reads x0 (tag=0) as the C-ABI int return -> exit(0). The static hand stub reads x1 (payload) via mov x0,x1 -> 42; the dyn path had no such adapter. Fix (Fable H1): a 24B+8pad C-ABI main trampoline at text offset 0 on the crt_handoff branch (stp/mov/bl real-main/mov x0,x1/ldp/ret) + redirect the main def to it (def_off=0, main_off=real body for the bl patch). Zero codegen change; static stub + pair ABI byte-identical. x86 link_elf_x86_64_ownstart has the identical gap (sibling follow-on).

title: fix(axis-③/arm64 rung-3): 16-align bss_vaddr_base — .bss LDST64 misalign on dyn path
body: the real root cause of the LDST64 $sec_0_4 rc=2: bss_vaddr_base = data_vaddr + len(data_bytes) was not aligned. A .bss section symbol (seg 2) resolves to bss_vaddr_base + value; an ldr x,[sec,:lo12:] needs an 8-aligned target. Road A dyn blobs (interp /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 = 27B odd) left len(data_bytes) odd -> odd bss_vaddr_base -> rc=2. Fix: 16-align data_bytes before bss_vaddr_base. Static path unaffected (ended at 8-padded GOT). convergence elf-arm64-hexa-1 corrected (section-base align was the wrong locus).

title: fix(axis-③/arm64 rung-3): 16-align obj section bases (crt1-prepend LDST64 misalign)
body: concat pass 16-aligns each obj rodata/data section base. crt1 prepend (dyn path) shifted a later obj section by crt1 byte size; non-8-aligned shift made an ldr x,[sec,:lo12:] (LDST64_ABS_LO12_NC) against $sec_N_4 fail the scale-3 alignment check (_apply_arm64_reloc rc=2). data_vaddr is 0x10000-aligned so 16-aligned blob offset gives 16-aligned section vaddr (max AArch64 LDST). Static path unaffected (never prepended); --linker=hexa opt-in.

title: fix(axis3 L2): own-start stub populates _hxlcl_environ from envp — env() works in own-linked binaries
body: axis-③ L2: own-start _start stub now populates _hxlcl_environ from the entry-stack envp, so env()/getenv work in an own-linked (--linker=hexa, crt-less) binary. Root cause: the hand stub bypasses runtime.a asm _start/_hx_start_c (hxlcl_environ=envp) + synthesizes .init_array zero-trip → _hxlcl_environ .bss cell stays NULL → hxlcl_getenv returns "" for every key → cc_self cant read HEXA_PREBUILT_RUNTIME/HOME/HEXA_BACKEND (self-host blocker). Fix (linker-only, elf_x86_64.hexa link_elf_x86_64_ownstart): pre-scan objs for a DEFINED _hxlcl_environ; if present, emit a 35-byte v4 stub (lea rdx,[rsp+rdi*8+16] envp + mov [rip+d32],rdx) and hand-patch the d32 to the .bss cell vaddr after the data blob is final; else the plain 23-byte stub (no-runtime unit-test links byte-identical). Shipping --emit=obj path untouched (system CC links; runtime own _start sets environ). Design: Fable; root cause via disasm falsifying the workflows codegen-tag-drop theory.

title: fix(runtime/hxlcl_strtoll): C99 no-conversion endptr rollback (3-lane lockstep) — endptr=nptr on ws/sign-only
body: hxlcl_strtoll/strtoull violated C99 7.22.1.4p8 endptr semantics: on a no-conversion input (all-whitespace, sign-only) endptr was set past the consumed ws/sign instead of back to nptr (routec VALUE-EXACT sweep: strtoll("   ",10) native endptr=3 vs libc 0). Root cause is the FROZEN FLOOR (self/runtime.c unconditional *endptr=s), byte-faithfully ported to the native. 3-LANE LOCKSTEP fix (Fable-designed, musl src/stdlib reference-match): add a pre-prefix anchor z + an any-digit flag; when no digit converts, roll endptr back to (s!=z ? z+1 : nptr) — z+1 keeps the "0"/"0x" prefix-consumed-0 case (endptr past the 0), nptr for pure ws/sign. Value always 0 (endptr-only). Lanes: emitter self/runtime_emit_full.hexa (shipping runtime.c strtoll+strtoull), native stdlib/runtime/hxlcl_core.hexa (Route C, strtoll+strtoull), shim frozen-branch self/runtime_core_hxlcl_shim_emit.hexa (strtoll). Side-fixes 2 latent caller bugs (hexa_pinned_epoch mis-pinning SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH="   " to 0; to_int edge cases converge to intended throw-on-non-integer). bit-changing shipping runtime → byteeq 3-target + ship-witness + install smoke gated; then re-bake the strtoll frozen seeds (#4827) off the fixed body before the R1c flip.

title: fix(tool/routec_strtoll_verify): measure strtoll in isolation — address-range [B] + provider-link [C], catches value divergence
body: The [B]/[C] steps could never measure hxlcl_strtoll: emit is a single .text section so objcopy --keep-global-symbol leaves sibling math-kernel code (hxlcl_log/exp/sin/cos) in the object, charging strtoll for their _hx_* + transitive deps → [B] false SELF_CONTAINED=NO (18 relocs) and [C]永 LINK_FAIL. Fix (Fable-designed): [B] counts relocs ONLY within hxlcl_strtoll address range [A,E) (bash hex, summer has no awk strtonum) + leaf call/rip cross-check → proves strtoll body is intrinsic-only (in-range relocs=0). [C] links strtoll_only.o + loose shim_on.o (hxlcl_malloc, no strtoll) + the whole canonical runtime.a as an archive (resolves _hx_* + transitive on-demand) with --allow-multiple-definition (native strtoll wins loose-first, _start→C CRT; the value MISMATCH it surfaces proves native — not libc — is under test, ruling out false-PASS). MEASURE-ONLY, byteeq-neutral. Now RUNS the value sweep and CAUGHT a real native endptr divergence (strtoll all-whitespace: native endptr=3 vs libc 0) — the flip gate works.
